headline: Energy Holds the Line as Selling Fans Out Across Growth Names
body_html:
Midway through Thursday's session, the tape is broadly negative, with decliners outnumbering advancers 345 to 204 across the tracked universe. Energy is the lone sector in positive territory, up 0.72%, drawing a clear bid as oil prices firm on geopolitical caution surrounding Iran-Oman diplomatic talks. Healthcare is roughly flat at minus 0.06%, but every other pocket of the market is lower, with Consumer and Homebuilders bearing the heaviest losses at minus 1.65% and minus 1.53% respectively.

Software and Semiconductors are each under pressure — down 1.22% and 0.99% — though the day's standout story on the upside is discrete chipmaker Diodes Incorporated, surging 12.49% to lead all gainers. Liquidity Services and Encompass Health are also sharply higher, up roughly 12% and 11% respectively, suggesting earnings-driven pockets of strength are available even in a risk-off tape. Parker-Hannifin's 9.13% advance is a notable bright spot within a struggling Industrials sector.

On the downside, Universal Technical Institute and LegalZoom.com have cratered roughly 30% and 28% respectively, while Datadog and Western Digital are each off more than 15%. Into the close, watch whether the Iran-deal headline flow accelerates — oil's resilience today is the market's clearest tell on geopolitical sentiment.

briefs.headline: Iran Tensions Keep Oil Bid Alive Mid-Session
briefs.body: Crude prices are holding gains as traders weigh the possibility of a diplomatic breakthrough between Iran and Gulf intermediaries against the risk of escalation. Houthi attacks on Saudi shipping have kept the risk premium elevated, and oil-linked equities are the clearest beneficiary in today's otherwise defensive tape.

briefs.headline: Diodes Incorporated Vaults 12% to Lead the Universe
briefs.body: The discrete semiconductor maker is the session's top percentage gainer, surging 12.49% amid what appears to be a significant earnings or guidance catalyst. The move stands in contrast to the broader semiconductor sector's 0.99% decline, underscoring how company-specific results are cutting through macro headwinds on a name-by-name basis.

briefs.headline: Universal Technical Institute Suffers a Session-Worst Collapse
briefs.body: Shares of the vocational-education provider are down nearly 30% mid-session, making it the steepest decliner in the tracked universe. The move signals a severe disappointment — likely tied to enrollment trends or forward guidance — and is dragging on the broader Consumer sector, already the worst-performing group today at minus 1.65%.

briefs.headline: European Equities Reach Record as Iran Optimism Lifts Sentiment Abroad
briefs.body: Across the Atlantic, European indices climbed to an all-time high during their session, lifted by a combination of solid corporate earnings and measured optimism that US-Iran diplomacy may yield progress. The divergence with softer US intraday action suggests global investors are pricing in a deal scenario that domestic markets have not yet fully embraced.

briefs.headline: Defense-Tech Funding Surge Continues With Hadrian's $8 Billion Valuation
briefs.body: Hadrian, a precision-manufacturing startup serving the defense industry, has secured fresh funding that values the company at close to eight billion dollars. The raise reflects sustained investor appetite for defense-adjacent technology as geopolitical instability drives government procurement demand, a theme that is also supporting broader Industrials names like Parker-Hannifin on the tape today.

briefs.headline: Dollar Ticks Higher as Markets Parse Iran Deal Odds and Await Payrolls
briefs.body: The greenback edged up in currency markets Thursday as traders balanced uncertainty over a potential Iran accord against anticipation of upcoming payrolls data. The dollar's modest strength is acting as a modest headwind for risk assets, reinforcing the cautious tone that has kept breadth negative and growth sectors — particularly Software and Consumer — under pressure through midday.
